purpose: Prove that separately executed AI sessions can repair bounded RCL-owned compiler lowering semantics from hidden mutations without seeing canonical compiler files or oracle edits.
rules: Each generator receives only mutated RCL compiler candidates, the semantic invariant and observed verifier result.
Canonical compiler files, mutation implementation and oracle edits are absent from the generator workspace.
Each trial runs in a fresh ephemeral read-only session that ignores project rules and user configuration.
The evaluator applies only the exact file/old/new edit returned through the frozen JSON Schema.
The generator cannot edit tests, thresholds, evidence, authority policy or the authoritative repository.
Every saved repair must restore byte-identical canonical RCL compiler sources and pass compiler semantic replay.
The three canonically restored candidates share one native C0/C1/C2 fixed-point witness because their input bytes are identical.
Three unique generator sessions, three successful deterministic replays and a GitHub-hosted Linux plus Windows replay are required.

trials.intent: Repair binary expression lowering so addition emits the canonical ADD opcode while preserving the general compiler path.
Repair binary expression lowering so less-than-or-equal emits its distinct canonical opcode without weakening comparison coverage.
Repair the final greater-than-or-equal branch while preserving the explicit unknown-operator fallback boundary.

evidenceBoundary: This contract proves bounded independent repair of three checked-in RCL compiler opcode-lowering mutations plus a shared native compiler fixed point. It does not prove arbitrary compiler evolution, whole-runtime self-hosting, unrelated K400 cells or K400 completion.
